clue.text: Start of an attack

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the beginning of something and an assault, as in the onset of enemy troops.

clue.text: Butterfly operating all over the place

indicators.note: scattered everywhere, so the letters of the word beside it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone notes a butterfly flitting about, working away everywhere at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' rearranges OPERATING into the name of a common European butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange-tip is a white butterfly whose male has bright orange wingtips, a common species in Britain.

clue.text: One follows smash-hit with operational research

parts.note: a smash hit is a great success
OR is the standard abbreviation for operational research

explanation.surface: A hit show is followed up with a scientific study of how it works.
explanation.definitionFit: A successor is someone who comes after another, taking over a role.

clue.text: Drinks for kids

explanation.definitionFit: Small measures of whisky and small children share this word.

clue.text: Cooked flaring, as in bifteck?

indicators.note: food cooked is changed in form, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A chef flambes something in a French kitchen, with steak on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' rearranges FLARING and AS. Bifteck is the French borrowing of English 'beefsteak', a classic example of mixed-language usage, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Franglais is French peppered with English loanwords, and bifteck is an instance of it.

clue.text: House pet, long-admired?

parts.note: a business house is a company or firm
a teacher's pet is the favourite

explanation.surface: A family's cherished house animal, loved for years.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held in steady, lasting esteem is a constant preference, admired for a long time.

clue.text: Travel by rail can be so dreadfully messy!

parts.note: to go is to travel
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A grumble that train journeys can be grubby and unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Gory describes something covered in blood, which is horribly messy.

clue.text: Humble tar residue

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Lowly leftover tar, as if describing sticky deposits on a road.
explanation.definitionFit: To humble someone is to embarrass or shame them, the verb sense.

clue.text: President, transported all around, is exhausted

indicators.note: the word for transported surrounds the abbreviation for the head of state

parts.note: transported means sent

explanation.surface: A head of state, driven around everywhere, ends up tired out.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent means used up or worn out, like an exhausted runner.

clue.text: A Caledonian cravat

parts.note: Caledonia is the Latin name for Scotland, so a Caledonian is a Scot

explanation.surface: A Scottish neckerchief.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascot is a broad neck scarf, a type of cravat worn at formal occasions.

clue.text: Bang-on-time news coverage

parts.note: a bang is a loud report, like a gunshot
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: News reporting that is perfectly punctual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bang-on' looks like British slang for exactly right; split it and 'Bang' is the noise, while 'on' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Reportage is journalism, the reporting of events in the press.

clue.text: Patina's re-applied, majestically, in meticulous style

indicators.note: applied again in a new way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word read with its s as a letter
majestically means in a kingly manner

explanation.surface: A restorer redoes the old sheen on a royal piece with great care.
explanation.walkthrough: 're-applied' is the anagram signal; here the 's of Patina's counts as a letter rather than marking a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Painstakingly means with great care and attention to detail, the same as meticulously.

clue.text: Leaves cracks

definitions.meaning: attempts or tries, as in having a crack at something

explanation.definitionFit: Goes means departs, and as a plural noun means attempts or turns.

clue.text: Join a very loud team

parts.note: FF is fortissimo in musical notation
IX is nine in Roman numerals, the size of a baseball team

explanation.surface: An invitation to sign up with a noisy sports side.
explanation.walkthrough: The team here is nine players (as in baseball), IX in Roman numerals, rather than the cricket or football eleven, XI.
explanation.definitionFit: To affix is to attach or fasten one thing to another.

clue.text: This last cabin not open for business?

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word this is used

parts.note: a hut is a small cabin

explanation.surface: A remark that this final hut is closed to customers.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop that is shut is closed and not trading.

clue.text: Triangle on a potter's table?

parts.note: the potter is a snooker player potting balls, and the triangle racks up the reds at the start of each game

explanation.definitionFit: In snooker the wooden triangle is called the frame, and one game is also a frame.

clue.text: Forger's block

parts.note: a blacksmith forges metal, hammering it on a heavy iron block, rather than faking banknotes

explanation.definitionFit: An anvil is the iron block on which a smith hammers hot metal.

clue.text: Fights in bootless fashion

parts.note: bootless means fruitless, not barefoot, so this describes efforts that gain nothing

explanation.definitionFit: To try hard without success is to make a struggle that achieves nothing.

clue.text: Mass Caine mutiny is always new to these people

indicators.note: a mutiny overturns order, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A whole crowd of Michael Caine's crew rises up, a nod to the film The Caine Mutiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mutiny' rearranges MASS and CAINE. People who cannot remember anything find everything new.
explanation.definitionFit: Those with amnesia have lost their memory, so every experience seems fresh to them.

clue.text: West Wensleydale out of beer, surprisingly, for the happy couple

indicators.note: something surprising is unexpected, so these letters come out in an unexpected order
the beer word is taken out of the cheese name

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire Dales pub has run dry, yet the bride and groom still celebrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes ALE from WENSLEYDALE (a Yorkshire dale, and a cheese) leaving WENSLEYD; with W, 'surprisingly' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Newly-weds are a couple recently married, conventionally described as happy.

clue.text: Tour map in Elba opened up for this walkabout

indicators.note: unfolded and spread out, so these letters are laid out anew

explanation.surface: A visitor unfolds a map on the island of Elba to plan a stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opened up' rearranges TOUR MAP IN ELBA, all thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A perambulation is a leisurely walk around a place, a stroll or walkabout.

clue.text: Small nail used for rail notice

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former UK national railway
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: A tack pinning up a poster at a railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: BR is British Rail, the old nationalised British railway operator.
explanation.definitionFit: A brad is a thin wire nail with a small head.

clue.text: Alloy fuse

definitions.meaning: a mixture of metals, a combination

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means a mixture such as an alloy, and as a verb to merge or combine.

clue.text: This lighting is very bad!

parts.note: reads as a complaint about dim lamps, but means setting fire to property, a crime

explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the criminal act of deliberately setting fire to a building.

clue.text: End of motorway illuminated all round

indicators.note: the word for illuminated surrounds the road abbreviation

parts.note: illuminated means lit
motorway gives MI

explanation.surface: The final stretch of a motorway is lit up throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is a boundary or end point beyond which something cannot go.

clue.text: Catch a glimpse of English mole, perhaps

parts.note: a mole is an undercover agent, one kind of spy

explanation.surface: Spotting a burrowing animal in an English garden.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to see something briefly or at a distance.

clue.text: Still one follows the elusive mountain creature

indicators.note: the numeral comes after the first word in the answer

parts.note: still means yet, as in not yet
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is still tracking the elusive beast of the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti is the abominable snowman, a legendary creature said to roam the Himalayas.

clue.text: Polite cough taken up by a seamstress

definitions.meaning: a little throat-clearing noise to attract attention
read as two words, a single fold of fabric a dressmaker shortens

explanation.definitionFit: The cough is the throat-clearing sound, and split in two it is a single turned-up edge that a dressmaker shortens.

clue.text: Great tailless geese, cooked as Paschal gift

indicators.note: cooked food is transformed, so these letters are reordered
the bird word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Big geese, beheaded and roasted for a holiday feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' cuts the end letter from GEESE, leaving GEES; 'cooked' rearranges GREAT and GEES. Paschal means relating to Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate egg is the traditional present at the Christian spring festival, Paschal meaning of that feast.

clue.text: Lift provides endless enchantment

indicators.note: the word for enchantment loses its final letter

parts.note: heaven is bliss or delight, a state of enchantment

explanation.surface: An elevator ride that offers eternal delight.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to raise something heavy with effort.

clue.text: Delicate surgery-yet Dr isn't involved!

indicators.note: tangled up, so these letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A tricky operation, but surprisingly no doctor takes part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges YET, DR and ISNT. Despite the joke, a dentist is a doctor of sorts, but the surface pretends otherwise.
explanation.definitionFit: Dental work on teeth and gums is a fine, careful form of surgery.

clue.text: Maker of laws some break on Sunday?

indicators.note: in an across entry the abbreviation sits next on the right
breaking something smashes it, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A remark that some people break the rules on the Sabbath.
explanation.definitionFit: Moses brought the Ten Commandments to the Israelites, the biblical lawgiver.
